convention: The page opens on a hero: big headline, a subline, one button, one image.
why it is this kind: Habit. Nothing a visitor needs depends on this order.

convention: The headline is a slogan about the person or the product.
why it is this kind: Habit. A fact, a question or an action can open a page.

convention: Navigation is a horizontal bar at the top with four to six links.
why it is this kind: Habit. Findability matters (see F09); the bar is one way to get it.

convention: The site is a stack of full-width sections scrolled top to bottom.
why it is this kind: Habit inherited from landing-page templates.

convention: Sections run About, Services, Work, Testimonials, Contact.
why it is this kind: Template order, not a reader's order.

convention: Content sits in one centred column with equal margins.
why it is this kind: Habit. Asymmetric grids read fine.

convention: Repeating items are cards in a three-column grid.
why it is this kind: The single most generated layout; a list, a table or a timeline carries the same items.

convention: Every section has a small eyebrow label above its heading.
why it is this kind: Generated-page tell; adds nothing a heading lacks.

convention: The call to action is a filled pill button that says Book or Get started.
why it is this kind: The action must be findable (F01, F09); its shape and wording are free.

convention: Contact is a name, email and message form at the bottom of the page.
why it is this kind: The visitor needs a way to reach out (F07); the form is one way.

convention: Social proof is a row of logos or quote cards with headshots.
why it is this kind: Credibility matters; this format of it is habit.

convention: The footer holds columns of links, social icons and a copyright line.
why it is this kind: Habit.

convention: Photos are rectangles with rounded corners.
why it is this kind: Habit.

convention: The person appears in one polished portrait near the top.
why it is this kind: Habit. Process, hands, crowds or places can introduce a person.

convention: The site is the same for every visitor on every visit.
why it is this kind: Habit. Varying it is fine if every visitor still finds the core path (F08, F09).

convention: The site looks the same at every hour and season.
why it is this kind: Habit.

convention: The site is either several pages joined by a menu or one long page.
why it is this kind: Structure is free as long as URLs and back work (F03).

convention: Text is one sans-serif family at standard sizes.
why it is this kind: Habit.

convention: Every section fades up as it scrolls into view.
why it is this kind: Generated-motion tell; motion should match how often it is seen.

convention: The background is a flat colour or a soft gradient.
why it is this kind: Habit.

convention: The visitor stays anonymous and is never asked anything until the form.
why it is this kind: Habit. Asking first is fine if it is optional and fast.

convention: The person is described in a bio paragraph.
why it is this kind: Habit. Their own words, a record or a map can describe them.

convention: The site shows finished, polished outcomes and hides the process.
why it is this kind: Habit.

convention: Past work is a grid or list sorted newest first.
why it is this kind: Habit. Place, theme or audience can order it.

convention: A booking is a generic form and the reply comes later by email.
why it is this kind: The request must be confirmed (F13); waiting blind is habit.

convention: The site is a destination. The visitor takes nothing away.
why it is this kind: Habit. A file, a date, a card or a text can leave with them.

convention: Time is absent: no now, no next, no calendar.
why it is this kind: Habit.

convention: Everything is read silently. There is no voice or sound.
why it is this kind: Habit, as long as sound never autoplays (F14).

convention: Everything is visible at once. Nothing is earned or revealed by doing.
why it is this kind: Habit, as long as content stays reachable (F15).

convention: The whole site speaks to one audience in one tone.
why it is this kind: Habit. Organizers, listeners and peers want different things.

convention: Video sits in a player box with a play button.
why it is this kind: Habit.

convention: The path ends at a thank-you message after the form.
why it is this kind: Habit. What happens after the ask is free.

convention: The site's structure mirrors the org chart: one section per role or organization.
why it is this kind: Habit. A visitor's question is a different structure.

convention: Social links send the visitor away to other platforms.
why it is this kind: Habit.

convention: Rates, availability and logistics hide behind Inquire.
why it is this kind: Habit, sometimes a business choice; showing them is allowed.

convention: Scrolling is vertical.
why it is this kind: Habit, as long as every input still reaches the content (F15).

convention: Navigation labels are nouns: About, Work, Contact.
why it is this kind: Habit. Verbs or questions name what the visitor wants.

convention: Everyone enters through the same home page.
why it is this kind: Habit. Deep links per purpose are allowed.

convention: The designer picks one colour theme for all conditions.
why it is this kind: Habit.

convention: Credibility comes from the person describing themselves.
why it is this kind: Habit. Others' accounts, records and artifacts can carry it.

convention: Links look like links and buttons look like buttons.
why it is this kind: Brutalist Web Design rule 3, the one generated pages break first (apps/ux-engine/research/04-constraints-and-tells.md).

convention: Only links and buttons respond to clicks.
why it is this kind: Brutalist Web Design rule 2 (research/04).

convention: The back button works and every view has a shareable URL.
why it is this kind: Brutalist Web Design rule 4: breaking it shows contempt for the visitor (research/04).

convention: Body text meets contrast 4.5:1 and reads on every reasonable screen.
why it is this kind: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3; Brutalist rule 1 (research/04).

convention: Everything works by keyboard and focus is visible.
Motion reduces under prefers-reduced-motion: keep opacity and colour, drop transforms.
why it is this kind: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.3; claude-design-kit CLAUDE.md (reduce, not delete).

convention: Every form field has a visible label and errors say what to fix.
why it is this kind: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.1 and 3.3.2; no placeholder as a label.

convention: Within a few seconds a first-time visitor knows whose site it is and what they can do there.
why it is this kind: ux-engine CLAUDE.md first-look intent; ux-viewer checks it blind.

convention: The main action can be reached from anywhere without hunting.
why it is this kind: The visitor came to do one thing; ux-gen intent primary_action.

convention: Content shows without a long wait.
why it is this kind: Brutalist Web Design rule 7: performance is a feature (research/04).

convention: Text is real text: selectable, searchable, translatable.
why it is this kind: Screen readers, search and translation all read text, not pixels.

convention: Touch targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, 44 for primary actions.
why it is this kind: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 sets 24; 44 is the common platform guideline.

convention: After an action the visitor sees that it worked: sent, booked, saved.
why it is this kind: Nielsen heuristic 1, visibility of system status.

convention: Nothing plays sound on its own.
why it is this kind: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.2.

convention: Every piece of content is reachable by a standard input: scroll, tab, tap.
why it is this kind: Brutalist Web Design rule 5, reworded so scroll direction stays free (research/04).
